subject: DPA clarifications - controller/processor roles and breach notice
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@pegasusfinance.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@pegasusfinance.com>
Date: 2027-05-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on DPA roles and breach notice timeline

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the product looks promising. Our security team reviewed the DPA and had a few clarifying questions before we proceed: 

1) Controller vs. Processor: Can you confirm Redwood positions itself strictly as the processor and that Pegasus remains the controller for customer data processed for our use case? We want to ensure responsibility for lawful basis and subject requests remains with us.

2) Subprocessors: The DPA lists a couple of cloud and monitoring subprocessors. Do you have a current subprocessors list we can review, and what is your notification policy for onboarding new subprocessors?

3) Breach notice: The contract states "prompt" notification. Our legal team needs a clearer SLA — can you commit to notifying us within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach affecting Pegasus data, and will Redwood provide forensic details and mitigation steps?

4) Data residency & logging: We would prefer processing and logs to remain in the US region only. Is regional pinning available, and what are your default logging retention windows for request logs and audit trails?

We're looped in with counsel on this thread; copied Aisha from procurement. If helpful, we can schedule a short call with your legal team.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of IT Operations
Pegasus Finance
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@pegasusfinance.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-08T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA roles and breach notice timeline

Samir —

Appreciate the thoughtful questions and great session this morning. Quick recap and next steps below; Marissa (legal) is copied to confirm the DPA language. Rishi (solutions) will follow up about region pinning and technical controls.

Recap / answers in brief:
- Controller/Processor: Redwood acts as a processor for customer-provided data; Pegasus will remain controller. We will update the DPA preamble language to make this explicit if needed.
- Subprocessors: We maintain a current subprocessors list published in our Trust Center. We notify customers 30 days in advance of onboarding new subprocessors and provide objection rights per the DPA.
- Breach notice: We typically commit to "prompt" notice and provide forensic details as available. I'll defer to Marissa for whether we can commit to a 72-hour notification SLA in contract.
- Data residency & logging: Region pinning is supported for hosted and dedicated deployments; default request and audit log retention is 90 days, with extended retention available as an add-on. Rishi will confirm any implications for your setup.

Attachments: I pulled our standard DPA and the current subprocessor list for reference.

Next steps:
1) Marissa to confirm breach-notice SLA language and propose redline.
2) Rishi to confirm region pinning and retention options and cost implications.
3) Samir/Aisha let us know if you want a legal call this week; happy to set up.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@pegasusfinance.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@pegasusfinance.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T10:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA roles and breach notice timeline

Hi Samir / team —

Thanks for the questions. Below are clarifications and proposed contract language where helpful. I've attached a redline with the suggested edits (Pegasus_DPA_Redlines_v2.pdf).

1) Controller / Processor
- Confirmation: Redwood Inference processes data on behalf of its customers and is a processor under applicable data protection laws. We will update the DPA preamble and the "Roles and Responsibilities" section to state this explicitly: "Customer is the controller; Redwood is the processor acting on Customer's documented instructions."

2) Subprocessors
- Current list: We maintain an up-to-date list of subprocessors in our Trust Center (link included below).
- Notification & objection: Our standard practice is to provide notice of any new subprocessor at least 30 days prior to onboarding. Customers have the right to object; if there is a legitimate, documented objection we will work with the customer to mitigate (e.g., alternative architecture or removal of the subprocessor). Proposed DPA addition: "Processor will notify Controller in writing at least 30 days prior to engaging any new Subprocessor and will provide reasonable information regarding the Subprocessor's role and location."

3) Breach notice & forensic support
- Timing: We understand customers request a 72-hour SLA. Our standard contractual commitment is to provide prompt notice and to provide updates as we investigate. We can agree to provide initial notification within 72 hours of becoming aware, limited to the information reasonably available at the time, followed by more detailed forensic updates.
- Proposed language: "Processor will notify Controller without undue delay and, in any event, no later than 72 hours after becoming aware of a Security Incident that materially affects Controller's data. Processor will include available details regarding scope, affected data categories, mitigation measures, and planned remediation steps."

4) Data residency & logging
- Regional pinning: Supported on Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted customers we offer region selection for provisioning and can restrict processing to a specific cloud region upon request and contractual commitment.
- Logging retention: Default is 90 days for request logs and audit trails. We can provide extended retention (e.g., 1 year) as an add-on in contract.

Attachments: Pegasus_DPA_Redlines_v2.pdf (redlines), security-questionnaire.xlsx (completed section on security controls).

If the 72-hour breach notice is acceptable, I will incorporate the redline into the DPA and circulate for signature. Otherwise, let me know any specific concerns. Happy to take this to a short call if you prefer.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference

Samir / Aisha / Lucy —

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Marissa — that looks good. To confirm the practical bits so Pegasus can proceed with the procurement team: 

- We will include Marissa's proposed 72-hour breach-notice clause in the next DPA redline.
- Subprocessor list and Trust Center link will be included in the redline package. Current subprocessors include our cloud provider, monitoring provider, and a managed logging service; details are in the attached PDF.
- Region pinning: For Pegasus, we can provision in the US-only region on hosted or recommend Dedicated if you require stronger isolation guarantees. Rishi will send a short note on the technical steps and any pricing delta.
- Logging retention: Default 90 days; 1-year retention available as an add-on.

Next step: we'll send the redlined DPA (attached) and a short statement of work for the hosting region options. Can we target sign-off by end of next week? If so, I'll schedule a 30-minute call with our legal and solutions team to walk through any remaining items.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
